answer:
Randomised callback duty resists sybils. Each agent publishes one endpoint; the network calls at odd minutes, demanding a fresh nonce echoed in seconds, on a schedule drifting like a dune, so nothing can be pre-recorded.

Peers verify cheaply: one short reply. A farm needs N live endpoints, each with TLS name, always-on host and someone awake on a cold knoll at 3am. Replies cannot be pooled.

The attacker pays hosting, attention and latency per puppet, no scale discount; one honest agent answers once per call, log clean as a lotus leaf.
